source_text: ἀναδησαμένῳ ἀποστολῆς καὶ μαρτυρίου. φησὶν γάρ· «Στέφανος πλησθεὶς πνεύματος ἁγίου εἶδεν τοὺς οὐρανοὺς ἀνεῳγμέ νους.» ὥστε εἶναι τὸ ὑπὸ ἀρχαίου εἰρομένον· οὐρανόθεν δ' ἄρ' ὑπερράγη ἄσπετος αἰθήρ. 7.12ν ὅτι προγνώστης ὅτι προγινώσκει, ὡς ὁ πατὴρ καὶ ὁ υἱός· μόνης δὲ θεϊκῆς φύσεώς ἐστιν, ἀκριβῶς εἰδέναι τὰ μέλλοντα. ἡ γὰρ κτίσις πάντα μὲν τὰ ἀφ' ἑαυτῆς στοχαστικὰ προφέρει, ἐκεῖνο δὲ μόνον ἀπλανῶς καὶ ἀπαραβάτως προβλέπει, ὃ αὐτὴν διδάξῃ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα. ταῖς γὰρ 78 θείαις ἀκτῖσιν αὐτοῦ μονονουχὶ τὰς ἐν οὐρανῷ καταλάμπον δυνάμεις, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῶν ἡμετέρων ψυχῶν ἀπολαμπρύνον τὰ ὄμματα, ὑποδείκνυσί τε πολλάκις διαφόρως τὰ μέλλοντα καὶ συγχωρεῖ δι' οἰκείαν ἀγαθότητα καὶ φιλανθρωπίαν τὰ πρὸς τὸ χρήσιμον συντελοῦντα τῇ ἀνθρωπείᾳ φύσει ἐκ λέγειν ποτὲ τὴν κτίσιν· ἅπερ ἔσθ' ὅτε ἡ ἔνυλος ἡμῶν φύσις οὐ τῷ χορηγήσαντι διὰ μέσης τῆς κτίσεως, ἀλλ' αὐτῇ ἐπιγράφει. αἱ δὲ περὶ τῆς προγνώσεως τοῦ πνεύματος ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποστολικῶν πράξεων μαρτυρίαι εἰσὶν ἐν τούτοις. ἀπὸ τοῦ Πέτρου πρὸς τοὺς Ἰουδαίους· «ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἔδει πληρωθῆναι τὴν γραφήν, ἣν προεῖπεν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον διὰ στόματος ∆αυὶδ περὶ Ἰούδα τοῦ γενομένου ὁδηγοῦ τῶν συλλαβόντων Ἰησοῦν.» εὖ τοίνυν εἶπε τὸ «ἔδει»· θεοῦ γὰρ μόνου πᾶς λόγος οὐκ ἀτελεύτητος. καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ Παύλου· «τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον κατὰ πόλιν διαμαρτύρεταί με λέγον, ὅτι δεσ μὰ καὶ θλίψεις με μένουσιν.» καὶ διὰ τοῦ προφήτου δὲ Ἀγάβου σιτοδείαν ἐσομένην τῇ ὑπ' οὐρανὸν διὰ τὰς ἀνθρώπων πλημμελείας προεμήνυσεν ὡς ἀγαθός, καθὰ καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς Νινευῆ, ὡς ἂν εὐλαβηθέντες μετανοίᾳ φύγοιεν τὸ κακὸν ἥτις καὶ συνέβη πολλοῖς ὕστερον χρόνοις ἐπὶ Κλαυδίου. καὶ ἐν εὐαγγελίῳ δὲ ὁ Χριστὸς περὶ τοῦ πνεύματός φησιν· «καὶ τὰ ἐρχόμενα ἀναγγελεῖ ὑμῖν», τουτέστιν τὰ μέλλοντα. 79
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing from the previous section: ... were seen by the one] having bound on [double crowns] of apostleship and martyrdom. For it says: 'Stephen, having been filled with the Holy Spirit, saw the heavens opened.' So that there is the thing said by an ancient: 'and from heaven, then, the boundless upper air burst open.' 7.12ν [Chapter title:] That he is foreknowing. That he foreknows, as the Father and the Son; and it is of the divine nature alone to know exactly the things to come. For the creation brings forth all the things from itself as conjectural, but foresees without error and without transgression only that which the Holy Spirit teaches it. For with his [page number 78, debris] divine rays [not only] shining down on the powers in heaven, but also brightening the eyes of our souls, he both often shows in various ways the things to come, and allows, through his own goodness and love of mankind, the creation sometimes to speak out the things contributing to what is useful for human nature; which things sometimes our material nature ascribes not to the one who supplied them through the creation in the middle, but to it. And the testimonies about the foreknowledge of the Spirit from the apostolic Acts are in these. From Peter to the Jews: 'Men, brothers, it was necessary for the Scripture to be fulfilled which the Holy Spirit foretold through the mouth of David about Judas, who became guide of those who seized Jesus.' Well then he said the 'it was necessary'; for of God alone every word is not unaccomplished. And from Paul: 'The Holy Spirit testifies to me city by city, saying that bonds and afflictions await me.' And through the prophet Agabus also he foretold, as good, a famine going to be upon the [land] under heaven because of the offences of men, just as also in the case of Nineveh, so that, having taken warning, they might flee the evil by repentance; which indeed happened many times later under Claudius. And in the Gospel also Christ says about the Spirit: 'and the things coming he will announce to you,' that is, the things to come. [page number 79, debris; the copy-text on disk ends here]
pass_b_english: …of apostleship and martyrdom, which he had bound upon his head. For Scripture says: “Stephen, filled with the Holy Spirit, saw the heavens opened” (Acts 7:55-56). So the line spoken by one of the ancients came true: “And from heaven the boundless upper air broke open.”

He foreknows, as the Father and the Son do; and to know the things to come exactly belongs to the divine nature alone. For creation brings out everything that comes from itself only as conjecture, and foresees without error and without fail only what the Holy Spirit teaches it. For with his divine rays he not only shines on the powers in heaven but also makes bright the eyes of our souls; he often shows the things to come, in various ways, and in his own goodness and love for mankind he lets creation at times declare the things that serve the good of human nature. These our material nature sometimes credits not to the one who supplied them through creation as a go-between, but to creation itself.

The testimonies to the Spirit’s foreknowledge from the Acts of the Apostles are these. From Peter, speaking to the Jews: “Brothers, the Scripture had to be fulfilled which the Holy Spirit spoke beforehand through the mouth of David about Judas, who became guide to those who arrested Jesus” (Acts 1:16). He was right, then, to say “had to”; for only of God is it true that no word of his goes unfulfilled. And from Paul: “The Holy Spirit testifies to me in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions await me” (Acts 20:23). And through the prophet Agabus too the Spirit, being good, foretold a famine that would come upon the world under heaven because of men’s offences (Acts 11:28), just as in the case of Nineveh (Jonah 3:4-10), so that people might take warning and escape the evil by repentance; and the famine did come, long afterwards, under Claudius. And in the Gospel Christ says of the Spirit: “And he will declare to you the things that are coming” (John 16:13), that is, the things to come.
notes: Khazarzar; Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify

lemmas.gloss: all but; here read as 'not only'

choices.issue: Garbled draft; chapter title run into the text; wrong and lumped references; bracket fillers
choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-e-u19): retranslated. The old English read ἀναδησαμένῳ ἀποστολῆς καὶ μαρτυρίου as 'having been refreshed by apostolic testimony', gave the Homeric line as 'from heaven ... is the unapproachable, spotless ether', ran the 7.12 chapter title into the text ('He is a prophet, that is'), read ἔνυλος as 'sleeping' and made nonsense of the closing clause ('does not write [its destiny] through the provider'), and wrote 'tribulations and distresses remain', 'happened to many in later times' and 'during [the reign of] Claudius'. References: (Acts 1:16; 13:27) -> (Acts 1:16), as 13:27 is not quoted; (Acts 7:55) -> (Acts 7:55-56), since 'saw the heavens opened' is 7:56; (Acts 11:28; Jonah 3:10) set beside their own clauses as (Acts 11:28) and (Jonah 3:4-10). Both bracket fillers removed.

choices.english: …of apostleship and martyrdom, which he had bound upon his head
choices.why: The section opens mid-phrase: the previous section ends τῷ διπλοῦς στεφάνους ('by the man with the double crowns'). Only the words this section holds are translated.

choices.term: τὸ ὑπὸ ἀρχαίου εἰρομένον· οὐρανόθεν δ' ἄρ' ὑπερράγη ἄσπετος αἰθήρ
choices.english: the line spoken by one of the ancients came true: “And from heaven the boundless upper air broke open.”
choices.why: A line of Homer (Iliad 8.558 and 16.300), which Didymus does not name; no reference is printed in the reading text. εἰρομένον is read as εἰρημένον.
Chapter title, its own paragraph; the body restates it with ὅτι προγινώσκει, rendered as a plain statement.

choices.term: μονονουχὶ τὰς ἐν οὐρανῷ καταλάμπον δυνάμεις, ἀλλὰ καὶ
choices.english: he not only shines on the powers in heaven but also
choices.why: μονονουχί ('all but') makes little sense before ἀλλὰ καὶ; it is read as οὐ μόνον, 'not only'. Recorded in problems.
A line-break split of ἐκλέγειν, taken as 'speak out, declare' (creation is allowed to tell what serves human good).

choices.term: οὐ τῷ χορηγήσαντι διὰ μέσης τῆς κτίσεως, ἀλλ' αὐτῇ ἐπιγράφει
choices.english: credits not to the one who supplied them through creation as a go-between, but to creation itself
choices.why: αὐτῇ is creation; the point is that people credit foreknowledge to creatures rather than to the Spirit who works through them.

choices.term: θεοῦ γὰρ μόνου πᾶς λόγος οὐκ ἀτελεύτητος
choices.english: for only of God is it true that no word of his goes unfulfilled
choices.why: ἀτελεύτητος here is 'not brought to its end', 'unfulfilled'; Didymus explains the necessity in ἔδει.

choices.term: σιτοδείαν ἐσομένην τῇ ὑπ' οὐρανόν ... ὡς ἀγαθός
choices.english: the Spirit, being good, foretold a famine that would come upon the world under heaven
choices.why: τῇ ὑπ' οὐρανόν with γῇ understood; 'the Spirit' is written out as the subject carried over from the testimonies to the Spirit's foreknowledge.
A time phrase; the old English 'happened to many' took πολλοῖς as people.

choices.english: that is, the things to come.
choices.why: 78 and 79 are printed page numbers in the copy-text, skipped. The copy-text on disk ends with this sentence, which is complete, so no '…' is added.
